requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints` has no structural obligations, and it has no implementation edges, which is consistent with that.

I checked each clause for a required library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface:

- "every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint after the system prompt ... and another at the end of its last message". This describes the content of requests sent to the backend. A different internal design could add the checkpoints in any layer or with any data structure and send the same requests. The location of the code is discretionary.
- "Cache checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request". This is an observable property of the request.
- "For OpenAI ... the harness MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order. It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks." These are also constraints on the emitted requests. They do not prescribe how the harness is built.
- The condition "For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model support prompt caching" only says when the behavior applies. It names no interface through which that must be decided.
- The citation of `requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` is context only. Its own structural content, such as how prompts are assembled, belongs to that requirement.

Every clause therefore specifies observable request behavior. Tests would verify it, and the behavioral criterion covers that. No implementation root is needed.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each behavioral obligation of `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`.

**Explicit-checkpoint backends (Bedrock)**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` runs two requests against a Claude model. The second follows a reasoning turn.
  - For every request it asserts that `system` is the prompt text followed by one `cachePoint`.
  - It asserts that the last message ends in a `cachePoint`.
  - It asserts that the body holds exactly two `cachePoint` strings, so no extra or stale checkpoints remain.
- The "MUST NOT change the content of a request" obligation is covered. The same run against an uncached model (`fixture-uncached-model`) yields requests with no `cachePoint`. Each cached body, once `without_cache_points` strips the checkpoints, equals the plain body.
- The "when the backend and model support caching" condition is covered in both directions. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]` asserts `bedrock_caches` is true for Claude (including an ARN) and Nova models. It asserts false for Llama and the fixture model. The end-to-end test shows no checkpoints for the uncached model.
- The unit test also checks that `place_cache_checkpoints` changes only the cache option, including after a reasoning turn.

**OpenAI**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` makes two requests in one conversation.
  - It asserts that `instructions` and `tools` are identical across them.
  - It asserts that the second `input` begins with the first request's `input` unchanged, followed by the `function_call` and `function_call_output` in order.
  - It asserts via `assert_no_checkpoints` that neither request contains `cachePoint`, `cache_control`, or checkpoint block types.

The statement that checkpoints let a request reuse earlier content is the purpose of the checkpoints. It is not a separate observable obligation. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligations.

text: :::{req} cache_checkpoints
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.
For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
structural requirement review, behavioral requirement review, distributed
requirement review, example, citation review, and site review. A system prompt MUST be the same for
every assessment of its kind, so every placeholder whose value depends on the
subject MUST be in the subject message.
